summary: The legacy BIP70 merchant-name parser trusts an embedded one-byte string length and can read past the stored payment-request buffer.
evidence: Wallet transaction deserialization preserves arbitrary legacy PaymentRequest byte strings. When transaction details are opened, GetPaymentRequestMerchant locates two marker sequences, reads the following type and length without proving those bytes exist, and passes pr.data()+cn_pos with the unvalidated signed length to QString::fromUtf8. A truncated request or a claimed name longer than the remaining buffer therefore permits an out-of-bounds read in the GUI transaction-details path.
context: BIP70 ingestion is disabled for new URIs, but legacy payment-request records remain supported in wallet transaction deserialization and can be reached through restored or migrated wallet data.

summary: PSBT import checks file size through one stream and then performs an unbounded read through a second stream.
evidence: gotoLoadPSBT first opens and reads the selected path through GetFileSize with a 100 MiB cap, closes that stream, then reopens the path and assigns all bytes from istreambuf_iterator into a vector with no limit. A lower-trust local writer can replace or grow the selected file after the check, bypassing the intended cap and driving unbounded GUI memory consumption.
context: The attack requires local write control over the selected file or its directory during import, but the repository threat model explicitly includes adversarial local file inputs and symlink/race behavior.

summary: Qt RPC console redaction omits descriptor RPCs that accept and use private-key descriptors.
evidence: The console only redacts methods present in historyFilter, then displays and retains the resulting command text. importdescriptors accepts descriptor strings that can contain private keys, and descriptorprocesspsbt expands private descriptor material to sign inputs, but neither method appears in the filter. Commands containing xprv or WIF material therefore remain visible and retrievable in the console history after the wallet is relocked.
context: This is a local GUI disclosure, but it defeats an explicit control whose stated purpose is to keep private-key-handling commands out of console history.

summary: Transaction-history CSV export preserves formula-leading labels supplied through Bitcoin URIs.
evidence: The BIP21 parser accepts the label query value without excluding spreadsheet formula prefixes, WalletModel persists that label after a send, and TransactionView exports the label column. CSVModelWriter only doubles quote characters and wraps the value in quotes; it does not neutralize leading '=', '+', '-', or '@', which common spreadsheet applications may interpret as formulas when the user opens the exported history.
context: The path requires the user to accept a payment URI, complete a send, export transaction history, and open it in a formula-evaluating spreadsheet, so reachability is interaction-dependent.
